042/**
043 * Provides String based properties like {@link System#getProperty(String)} for default
044 * configuration of logging levels and output. Since Rainbow Gum is configuration agnostic
045 * LogProperties is a simple string key and string value interface to allow almost any
046 * configuration implementation. The only required method to implement is
047 * {@link #valueOrNull(String)} and thus LogProperties is a functional like interface but
048 * using {@link LogProperties#builder()} is preferred so that a
049 * {@linkplain #description(String) description} can be added.
050 * <p>
051 * If a custom {@link LogProperties} is not configured the default RainbowGum uses System
052 * properties.
053 * <p>
054 * The built-in properties to configure RainbowGum are modeled after <a href=
055 * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/docs/3.1.0/reference/html/features.html#features.logging">
056 * Spring Boot logging </a>
057 * <p>
058 * LogProperties should generally be accessed with {@link #forKey(String)} (see
059 * {@link LogProperty}) which will allow safe <em>programmatic</em> data conversion of the
060 * flat key values and useful error messages to users if the property cannot be mapped or
061 * is missing. For more <em>declarative</em> injection of properties see
062 * {@link LogConfigurable} which will generate builders that can use LogProperties.
063 * <p>
064 * Rainbow Gum treats {@value #SEP} in the keys as special separator analogous to
065 * JavaScript/JSON and various other configuration systems. Furthermore to work with a
066 * wide set of configuration systems once a property key has a value it is
067 * <strong>RECOMMENDED</strong> that there should not be other property key value with a
068 * key that is a prefix of the previously mentioned key. For example allowing two
069 * properties <code>logging.example=stuff</code>, <code>logging.example.a=A</code> is not
070 * recommended as <code>logging.example</code> is defined as a leaf. The exception to this
071 * rule is logging levels mapped to logger names for consistency with Spring Boot.
072 * <p>
073 * Rainbow Gum out of the the box supports parsing two formats into properties:
074 * {@link Properties} text, and {@link URI#getRawQuery()} percent encoded query
075 * parameters. The two different formats have different behavior for
076 * {@link #listOrNull(String)} and {@link #mapOrNull(String)}. If a custom format of
077 * LogProperties is created those two methods may need to be extended.
078 * <p>
079 * A convention used through out Rainbow Gum is to have the property names as constants as
080 * it makes documentation easier. These constants name are suffixed with
081 * <code>_PROPERTY</code> or <code>_PREFIX</code> the former being a fully qualified key
082 * that maybe parameterized and the latter being a partial key ending with
083 * "<code>.</code>". The fully qualified keys are like leaves on a tree.
084 * <p>
085 * Property keys can be parameterized by using
086 * {@link LogProperties#interpolateKey(String, Map)} and a general pattern is
087 * <code>logging.component.{name}.prop</code> where {@value #NAME} is a parameter. Many
088 * property constants use this to allow multiple configuration of components by name.
089 *
090 * <table class="table">
091 * <caption><strong>Built-in Property Patterns</strong></caption>
092 * <tr>
093 * <th>Property Pattern</th>
094 * <th>Description</th>
095 * </tr>
096 * <tr>
097 * <td>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = LEVEL</td>
098 * <td>Sets the level for the logger. If logger name is missing then it is considered the
099 * root logger. {@link Level#INFO} is the default level for the root logger.</td>
100 * </tr>
101 * <tr>
102 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} = {@link ChangeMode}</td>
103 * <td>Whether runtime changes are on for the configuration. Default is
104 * {@link ChangeMode#OFF}. When on, the loggers that may change are chosen with
105 * {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX}.</td>
106 * </tr>
107 * <tr>
108 * <td>{@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} + {@value #SEP} + logger = boolean |
109 * List&lt;{@link ChangeType}&gt;</td>
110 * <td>What may change at runtime for the logger and its children. By design RainbowGum
111 * does not allow loggers to change levels once initialized. Default is none. Has no
112 * effect unless {@value #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY} is on.</td>
113 * </tr>
114 * <tr>
115 * <td>{@value #ROUTES_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
116 * <td>A comma separated list of routes that should be enabled. If not set
117 * {@value LogRouter.Router#DEFAULT_ROUTER_NAME } is the default.</td>
118 * </tr>
119 * <tr>
120 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
121 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders associated with the route. If not set
122 * {@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} is used.</td>
123 * </tr>
124 * <tr>
125 * <td>{@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY} = <code>URI</code></td>
126 * <td>Looks up a publisher by URI scheme using the {@link LogPublisherRegistry}. The
127 * publisher is then configured by the other properties starting with
128 * {@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX}.</td>
129 * </tr>
130 * <tr>
131 * <td>{@value #PUBLISHER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
132 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
133 * <td>Configures the route's publisher of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
134 * example <code>logging.route.default.publisher.async.bufferSize</code>. The scheme is
135 * the one written in the URI, so <code>async</code> settings apply to whichever publisher
136 * is registered as <code>async</code>.</td>
137 * </tr>
138 * <tr>
139 * <td>{@value #APPENDERS_PROPERTY} = <code>List&lt;String&gt;</code></td>
140 * <td>A comma separated list of appenders that should be enabled. If not set
141 * {@value LogAppender#CONSOLE_APPENDER_NAME} is the default.</td>
142 * </tr>
143 * <tr>
144 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
145 * <td>Looks up an output by URI scheme using the {@link LogOutputRegistry}. The output is
146 * then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX}.</td>
147 * </tr>
148 * <tr>
149 * <td>{@value #APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY } = <code>URI</code></td>
150 * <td>Looks up an encoder by URI scheme using the {@link LogEncoderRegistry}. The encoder
151 * is then configured by the other properties starting with {@value #ENCODER_PREFIX}.</td>
152 * </tr>
153 * <tr>
154 * <td>{@value #OUTPUT_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
155 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
156 * <td>Configures the appender's output of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
157 * example <code>logging.appender.file.output.file.bufferSize</code>. An output built
158 * without an appender uses its own name in place of the appender's.</td>
159 * </tr>
160 * <tr>
161 * <td>{@value #ENCODER_PREFIX} + <code>scheme</code> + <code>.</code> +
162 * <code>propertyName</code></td>
163 * <td>Configures the appender's encoder of the type selected by the URI scheme, for
164 * example <code>logging.appender.console.encoder.json5.keyValues</code>. Each type has
165 * its own keys, so switching an appender's encoder leaves the other type's settings
166 * unread rather than misread. An encoder built without an appender uses its own name in
167 * place of the appender's.</td>
168 * </tr>
169 * <tr>
170 * <td>{@value #FILE_PROPERTY} = URI</td>
171 * <td>A URI or file path to log to a file. This is for Spring Boot compatibility.</td>
172 * </tr>
173 * </table>
174 *
175 * @see LogConfigurable
176 */
177public interface LogProperties {
178
179        /**
180         * properties separator.
181         */
182        static final String SEP = ".";
183
184        /**
185         * Logging properties prefix.
186         */
187        static final String ROOT_PREFIX = "logging" + SEP;
188
189        /**
190         * Controls direct fail-safe bootstrap diagnostics. {@code OFF} (also {@code false})
191         * is the default; {@code ERROR} dumps on build failure, while {@code INFO} also dumps
192         * after successful config builds. {@code ALL} (also {@code true}) additionally prints
193         * a {@link LogReporter} report after {@link RainbowGum#start()} starts the logging
194         * components. Read from system properties before properties providers run, so it
195         * remains available when loading configuration fails. The system property overrides
196         * {@link LogConfig.Builder#debug(LogConfig.DebugModeType)}.
197         */
198        static final String DEBUG_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "debug";
199
200        /**
201         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
202         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
203         */
204        static final String LEVEL_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "level";
205
206        /**
207         * Enabled level groups. The value should be a list of group names used on
208         * {@link #GROUP_PROPERTY}. This is to enable <a href=
209         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
210         * Spring Boot like Log Groups </a>. <em>Note that unlike Spring Boot groups are not
211         * enabled unless this property contains the group.</em>
212         */
213        static final String GROUPS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "groups";
214
215        /**
216         * Group property with list of logger names. The level of the group is set with
217         * <code>{@value #LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code> or on the router itself with
218         * <code>{@value #ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX} + .{name} = Level</code>. The group name can
219         * also be used in place of a logger name with {@value #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and
220         * {@value #CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX}. This is largely compatible with <a href=
221         * "https://docs.spring.io/spring-boot/3.3.2/reference/features/logging.html#features.logging.log-groups">
222         * Spring Boot Log Groups </a>.
223         * @see LevelResolver#parseLevel(String)
224         */
225        static final String GROUP_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "group.{name}";
226
227        /**
228         * Whether runtime changes are on: see {@link ChangeMode}.
229         */
230        static final String CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.mode";
231
232        /**
233         * The level threshold of events captured before Rainbow Gum is fully bound. Before
234         * Rainbow Gum is bound events are queued. By default events that are below
235         * <code>INFO</code> are not queued.
236         */
237        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_LEVEL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.level";
238
239        /**
240         * The level threshold of queued events reported to standard error before Rainbow Gum
241         * is bound. Defaults to <code>ERROR</code>.
242         */
243        static final String GLOBAL_QUEUE_ERROR_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.queue.error";
244
245        /**
246         * Whether output uses ANSI escape codes: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode}.
247         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AnsiMode#AUTO}.
248         */
249        static final String GLOBAL_ANSI_MODE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.ansi.mode";
250
251        /**
252         * Which kind of lock appenders use: see {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock}.
253         * Default is {@link LogConfig.Globals.AppenderLock#AUTO}.
254         */
255        static final String GLOBAL_APPENDER_LOCK_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.appender.lock";
256
257        /**
258         * Whether the logging path may use a {@link ThreadLocal}: see
259         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode}. Default is
260         * {@link LogConfig.Globals.ThreadLocalMode#ALLOW}.
261         */
262        static final String GLOBAL_THREAD_LOCAL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.threadLocal";
263
264        /**
265         * Opts every appender/encoder that has not been given an explicit choice into
266         * whatever this release currently believes is the best buffering/locking strategy for
267         * the platform the process is actually running on, instead of the fixed defaults
268         * ({@link LogAppender.AppenderType#LOCK_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER}, a
269         * {@link java.nio.charset.CharsetEncoder}-based encode) used otherwise. An explicit
270         * choice - programmatic ({@code appenderType(...)}, {@code useGetBytes(...)}) or via
271         * a more specific property ({@link LogAppender#APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY}) - always wins
272         * over this property; it only ever fills in what would otherwise be unset.
273         * <p>
274         * <strong>What "best" resolves to today, and why that is not a contract:</strong>
275         * currently this only has an effect under GraalVM native-image (detected the same way
276         * {@link LogAppender.AppenderType#AUTO_DETECT} is - see its javadoc), where it sets
277         * the default appender type to {@code AUTO_DETECT} (this benchmark's own measurements
278         * found {@code SYNCHRONIZED_THREAD_LOCAL_BUFFER} a real, repeatable win over the
279         * plain-JVM default there) and defaults text encoders to
280         * {@code String.getBytes(Charset)}-based encoding over the default
281         * {@code CharsetEncoder}-based one. On a plain JVM this property currently changes
282         * nothing at all - the measurements that motivated the native-image behavior above
283         * pointed the other way on HotSpot. None of this is a promise: as this project
284         * benchmarks more platforms, JDK versions, and encode strategies, what "optimize"
285         * resolves to on a given platform - including whether it does anything on a plain JVM
286         * at all - can and will change between releases without notice. Pin an explicit
287         * appender type/encoder strategy instead if a deployment needs a specific one to
288         * always be used.
289         */
290        static final String GLOBAL_OPTIMIZE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "global.optimize";
291
292        /**
293         * Key values namespace, for properties that configure where an event's key values
294         * come from.
295         */
296        static final String KEY_VALUES_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "keyvalues" + SEP;
297
298        /**
299         * A comma separated list of key value sources (the lowercase names of
300         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard}, for example
301         * <code>defaults,slf4j</code>) whose contributors are left out of every event's key
302         * values. A logging facade's own context store is still used for events logged
303         * through that facade, and {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor#clear()} still
304         * clears it according to
305         * {@link LogEventFactory.KeyValuesContributor.Source.Standard#clearWhenDisabled()}.
306         */
307        static final String KEY_VALUES_DISABLED_PROPERTY = KEY_VALUES_PREFIX + "disabled";
308
309        /**
310         * Maximum number of alerts {@link LogAlerts} holds in its ring buffer. Read once,
311         * from whatever {@link LogProperties} {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} has already
312         * resolved by the time it constructs {@link LogAlerts} - before any
313         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} runs.
314         * @see LogAlerts#DEFAULT_CAPACITY
315         */
316        static final String ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.capacity";
317
318        /**
319         * What {@link LogAlerts} does, once on {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig) start},
320         * if it has recorded at least one error alert and still has zero
321         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener}s registered - see
322         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction} for the three choices and
323         * {@link LogAlerts.UnobservedErrorsAction#DUMP} for the default.
324         */
325        static final String ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unobservedErrorsAction";
326
327        /**
328         * Alert level at which starting Rainbow Gum fails, like treating compiler warnings as
329         * errors: see {@link LogAlerts.FailLevel}. Unlike
330         * {@value #ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} it fails whether or not a
331         * {@link LogAlerts.Listener} is registered.
332         */
333        static final String ALERTS_FAIL_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.fail";
334
335        /**
336         * Alert level for property keys that were set but not read while starting: see
337         * {@link LogAlerts.UnusedKeyLevel}.
338         */
339        static final String ALERTS_UNUSED_KEY_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "alerts.unusedKey";
340
341        /**
342         * Per logger change properties prefix: see {@link ChangeType}.
343         */
344        static final String CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "change.logger";
345
346        /**
347         * Per logger caller info properties prefix: see {@link LogEvent.Caller.CallerType}.
348         * Independent of {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} and {@link #CHANGE_MODE_PROPERTY}:
349         * resolved through its own logger-name hierarchy walk, so a value here is never
350         * overridden by a more specific {@link #CHANGE_LOGGER_PREFIX} entry or vice versa.
351         */
352        static final String CALLER_LOGGER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "caller.logger";
353
354        /**
355         * Logging file property for default single file appending. The value should be a URI.
356         */
357        static final String FILE_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "file.name";
358
359        /**
360         * A common key parameter is called name.
361         */
362        static final String NAME = "name";
363
364        /**
365         * For properties keys that are parameterized with {@value #NAME} the name often used
366         * if not specified is: {@value #DEFAULT_NAME}.
367         */
368        static final String DEFAULT_NAME = "default";
369
370        /**
371         * Enabled Logging appenders. The value should be a list of names. This is equivalent
372         * to {@value #ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY} with name "default".
373         */
374        static final String APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "appenders";
375
376        /**
377         * Logging appender prefix for configuration.
378         */
379        static final String APPENDER_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "appender.{" + NAME + "}.";
380
381        /**
382         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's output, followed by the output's
383         * URI scheme, for example <code>logging.appender.{name}.output.file.</code>. Also
384         * used for an output built without an appender.
385         */
386        static final String OUTPUT_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "output.";
387
388        /**
389         * Prefix of the properties configuring an appender's encoder, followed by the
390         * encoder's URI scheme, for example
391         * <code>logging.appender.{name}.encoder.json5.</code>. Also used for an encoder built
392         * without an appender.
393         */
394        static final String ENCODER_PREFIX = APPENDER_PREFIX + "encoder.";
395
396        /**
397         * Output appender property.
398         */
399        static final String APPENDER_OUTPUT_PROPERTY = OUTPUT_PREFIX + "uri";
400
401        /**
402         * Encoder appender property.
403         */
404        static final String APPENDER_ENCODER_PROPERTY = ENCODER_PREFIX + "uri";
405
406        /**
407         * Appender flags. A list of flags (usually comma separated).
408         * @see AppenderFlag
409         */
410        static final String APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "flags";
411
412        /**
413         * Appender type (buffer/locking strategy). Unlike {@value #APPENDER_FLAGS_PROPERTY}
414         * this is a single value, not a list.
415         * @see LogAppender.AppenderType
416         */
417        static final String APPENDER_TYPE_PROPERTY = LogProperties.APPENDER_PREFIX + "type";
418
419        /**
420         * Routes enabled with names comma separated.
421         */
422        static final String ROUTES_PROPERTY = ROOT_PREFIX + "routes";
423
424        /**
425         * Route prefix for configuration.
426         */
427        static final String ROUTE_PREFIX = ROOT_PREFIX + "route.{" + NAME + "}.";
428
429        /**
430         * Prefix of the properties configuring a route's publisher, followed by the URI
431         * scheme of {@value #ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY}, for example
432         * <code>logging.route.{name}.publisher.async.</code>. Also used for a publisher built
433         * without a route.
434         */
435        static final String PUBLISHER_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "publisher.";
436
437        /**
438         * Logging publisher URI property.
439         */
440        static final String ROUTE_PUBLISHER_PROPERTY = PUBLISHER_PREFIX + "uri";
441
442        /**
443         * Appenders associated with a route comma separated.
444         */
445        static final String ROUTE_APPENDERS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "appenders";
446
447        /**
448         * Logging level properties prefix. The value should be the name of a
449         * {@linkplain java.lang.System.Logger.Level level}.
450         */
451        static final String ROUTE_LEVEL_PREFIX = ROUTE_PREFIX + "level";
452
453        /**
454         * Route flags.
455         */
456        static final String ROUTE_FLAGS_PROPERTY = ROUTE_PREFIX + "flags";
457
458        /**
459         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String)}.
460         * @param key property name.
461         * @return property value.
462         */
463        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key);
464
465        /**
466         * Analogous to {@link System#getProperty(String, String)} with the exception that the
467         * fallback cannot be null and the return cannot be null.
468         * @param key property name.
469         * @param fallback returned if the value is not found and may not be null.
470         * @return value found or fallback.
471         */
472        default String value(String key, String fallback) {
473                Objects.requireNonNull(fallback);
474                String v = valueOrNull(key);
475                if (v != null) {
476                        return v;
477                }
478                return fallback;
479        }
480
481        /**
482         * Gets a list or null if the key is missing and by default uses
483         * {@link #parseList(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
484         * as a list using {@link LogProperties#parseList(String)} but custom implementations
485         * may rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing
486         * configuration system.
487         * <p>
488         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
489         * and percent-encoded (<a href=
490         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
491         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
492         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
493         * logging.appenders=console,file
494         * </code></pre> resolves to <code>["console", "file"]</code>, and: <pre><code>
495         * logging.appenders=one%20two,three%2Cfour
496         * </code></pre> (a space and an escaped comma) resolves to
497         * <code>["one two", "three,four"]</code>. See {@link #parseList(String)} for empty
498         * elements.
499         * @param key property name.
500         * @return list or <code>null</code>.
501         * @apiNote the reason empty list is not returned for missing key is that it creates
502         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
503         */
504        default @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
505                String s = valueOrNull(key);
506                if (s == null) {
507                        return null;
508                }
509                return parseList(s);
510        }
511
512        /**
513         * Gets a map or null if the key is missing and by default uses
514         * {@link #parseMap(String)}. The default implementation will parse the string value
515         * as map using {@link LogProperties#parseMap(String)} but custom implementations may
516         * rely on their own parsing or the data type is built-in to the backing configuration
517         * system.
518         * <p>
519         * The returned map must iterate in a stable order, the same every time for the same
520         * configuration, preferably the order its entries were declared.
521         * <p>
522         * The default format is a single property value that is comma or ampersand separated
523         * <code>key=value</code> pairs, percent-encoded (<a href=
524         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
525         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded</a>) for entries needing to contain the separator
526         * or an equals sign, for example: <pre><code>
527         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=environment=prod,region=us-east
528         * </code></pre> resolves to
529         * <code>{"environment": "prod", "region": "us-east"}</code>, and: <pre><code>
530         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers=region=us%20east
531         * </code></pre> (a percent-encoded space) resolves to
532         * <code>{"region": "us east"}</code>.
533         * <p>
534         * When that property is not set, the map can instead be given as a list of its keys
535         * in <code>key.keys</code> and each value in <code>key.</code><em>mapKey</em>, which
536         * works with sources that only hold flat values such as system properties or
537         * environment variables, keeps the declared order, and needs no encoding: <pre><code>
538         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.keys=environment,region
539         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.environment=prod
540         * logging.appender.console.encoder.gelf.headers.region=us east
541         * </code></pre> A key listed without a value is an error.
542         * @param key property name.
543         * @return map or <code>null</code>.
544         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if a key listed in <code>key.keys</code> is empty
545         * or has no value.
546         * @apiNote the reason empty map is not returned for missing key is that it creates
547         * ambiguity so null is returned when key is missing.
548         */
549        default @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
550                String s = valueOrNull(key);
551                if (s == null) {
552                        return PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
553                }
554                return parseMap(s);
555        }
556
557        /**
558         * Suffix of the property listing a map's keys, see {@link #mapOrNull(String)}.
559         */
560        static final String MAP_KEYS_SUFFIX = "keys";
561
562        /**
563         * Visits this properties with visitor, by default just applying visitor to this and
564         * key directly. A composite/aggregate {@link LogProperties} (one backed by more than
565         * one underlying source) overrides this to recursively visit each of its members in
566         * order, returning the first non-<code>null</code> result - which member actually
567         * produced it is exactly what visitor is handed as its first argument, so a composite
568         * never needs to know anything about what visitor is trying to build (a raw value, a
569         * resolved property, or anything else); it just walks its members and stops at the
570         * first hit.
571         * @param <R> result type.
572         * @param key property key.
573         * @param visitor applied to (the member of this properties that ends up handling the
574         * visit, key); a <code>null</code> return means keep visiting.
575         * @return first non-<code>null</code> result, or <code>null</code> if nothing visited
576         * produced one.
577         */
578        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
579                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
580                return visitor.apply(this, key);
581        }
582
583        /**
584         * Searches up a {@value #SEP} separated path using this properties to check for
585         * values. The first value not missing (not <code>null</code>) will be returned.
586         * @param <T> result type
587         * @param root prefix.
588         * @param key partial key that will have prefix concated on each try of func.
589         * @param func convert function where <code>null</code> return means to keep
590         * searching.
591         * @return closest value or <code>null</code> if no value can be found.
592         * @see #findUpPathOrNull(String, Function)
593         */
594        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
595        default <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findOrNull(String root, String key,
596                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable T> func) {
597                return findUpPathOrNull(key, k -> func.apply(this, concatKey(root, k)));
598        }

601         * Starts resolving a property under key against this properties - the preferred entry

647        /**
648         * Abstract log properties builder.
649         *
650         * @param <T> builder.
651         * @apiNote this abstract class can largely be ignored hence why it is sealed.
652         */
653        public sealed abstract class AbstractBuilder<T> {
654
655                /**
656                 * description
657                 */
658                protected @Nullable String description = null;
659
660                /**
661                 * order
662                 */
663                protected int order = 0;
664
665                /**
666                 * rename key
667                 */
668                protected Function<String, String> renameKey = s -> s;
669
670                /**
671                 * fallbacks
672                 */
673                protected List<LogProperties> fallbacks = new ArrayList<>();
674
675                /**
676                 * Ignored.
677                 */
678                protected AbstractBuilder() {
679                }
680
681                /**
682                 * Add a fallback properties.
683                 * @param properties fallback not null.
684                 * @return this.
685                 */
686                public T with(LogProperties properties) {
687                        this.fallbacks.add(properties);
688                        return self();
689                }
690
691                /**
692                 * For returning this.
693                 * @return this builder.
694                 */
695                protected abstract T self();
696
697                /**
698                 * Description for properties.
699                 * @param description not null.
700                 * @return this.
701                 */
702                public T description(String description) {
703                        this.description = description;
704                        return self();
705                }
706
707                /**
708                 * When log properties are coalesced this method is used to resolve order. A
709                 * higher number gives higher precedence.
710                 * @param order order.
711                 * @return this.
712                 */
713                public T order(int order) {
714                        this.order = order;
715                        return self();
716                }
717
718                /**
719                 * Renames the key before it accesses function.
720                 * @param renameKey rename key function.
721                 * @return this.
722                 */
723                public T renameKey(Function<String, String> renameKey) {
724                        this.renameKey = renameKey;
725                        return self();
726                }
727
728                /**
729                 * Removes the prefix from a key before it accesses the underlying properties.
730                 * @param prefix to be removed from start of key.
731                 * @return this.
732                 */
733                public T removeKeyPrefix(String prefix) {
734                        return renameKey(k -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(k, prefix));
735                }
736
737        }

739        /**
740         * Builder for properties.
741         */
742        public final static class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
743
744                private @Nullable Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider = null;
745
746                private Builder() {
747                }
748
749                @Override
750                protected Builder self() {
751                        return this;
752                }
753
754                private Builder provider(Function<Builder, LogProperties> provider) {
755                        if (this.provider != null) {
756                                throw new IllegalArgumentException("from already set");
757                        }
758                        this.provider = provider;
759                        return this;
760                }
761
762                /**
763                 * Sets what is called on {@link LogProperties#valueOrNull(String)}.
764                 * @param function valueOrNull func.
765                 * @return this.
766                 */
767                public Builder fromFunction(@SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, @Nullable String> function) {
768                        return provider((b) -> new DefaultLogProperties(function,
769                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "function"), renameKey, order));
770                }
771
772                /**
773                 * Parses a string as {@link Properties}.
774                 * <p>
775                 * The parameter is the <strong>contents</strong> of a properties file, not a
776                 * resource, path, or file name. Passing a name such as
777                 * {@code "logging.properties"} does not load that file; it is parsed as a single
778                 * key with an empty value.
779                 * @param properties properties content as a string, for example
780                 * {@code "logging.level=INFO"}.
781                 * @return this.
782                 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum core does not read resources from the filesystem or the
783                 * classpath. If external properties are needed, it is the caller's responsibility
784                 * to read them into a string (or use a module that does, like
785                 * {@code rainbowgum-simple-props}).
786                 */
787                public Builder fromProperties(String properties) {
788                        if (description == null) {
789                                description = "PROPERTIES_STRING";
790                        }
791                        return fromFunction(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties)::get);
792                }
793
794                /**
795                 * Parses a string as a URI query string. If the URI has no query portion then it
796                 * will be equivalent to empty properties.
797                 * @param uri percent encoded uri with separator as "<code>&amp;</code>" and key
798                 * value separator of "<code>=</code>".
799                 * @return this.
800                 */
801                public Builder fromURIQuery(URI uri) {
802                        String query = uri.getRawQuery();
803                        return provider((b) -> queryToProperties(query,
804                                        Objects.requireNonNullElse(description, "URI_QUERY(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")")));
805                }
806
807                private MultiMapProperties queryToProperties(@Nullable String query, String description) {
808                        Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
809                        if (query == null) {
810                                multiMap = Map.of();
811                        }
812                        else {
813                                multiMap = parseMultiMap(query);
814                        }
815                        var properties = new MultiMapProperties(multiMap, description, renameKey, order);
816                        return properties;
817                }
818
819                /**
820                 * Builds LogProperties based on builder config.
821                 * @return this.
822                 */
823                public LogProperties build() {
824                        var f = this.provider;
825                        if (f == null) {
826                                if (!fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
827                                        return LogProperties.of(fallbacks);
828                                }
829                                throw new IllegalStateException("from was not set");
830                        }
831
832                        var first = f.apply(this);
833                        if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
834                                return first;
835                        }
836                        List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
837                        combined.add(first);
838                        combined.addAll(fallbacks);
839                        return LogProperties.of(combined);
840                }
841
842                static abstract class AbstractLogProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
843
844                        protected final String description;
845
846                        protected final Function<String, String> renameKey;
847
848                        protected final int order;
849
850                        public AbstractLogProperties(String description, Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
851                                super();
852                                this.description = description;
853                                this.renameKey = renameKey;
854                                this.order = order;
855                        }
856
857                        @Override
858                        public int order() {
859                                return this.order;
860                        }
861
862                        @Override
863                        public String description(String key) {
864                                String rename = renameKey.apply(key);
865                                return descriptionForKey(description, rename);
866                        }
867
868                        @Override
869                        public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
870                                out.append(description);
871                        }
872
873                        @Override
874                        public String toString() {
875                                return getClass().getSimpleName() + "[description='" + description + "', " + "order=" + order + "]";
876                        }
877
878                }
879
880                private static final class DefaultLogProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
881
882                        private final Function<String, @Nullable String> func;
883
884                        DefaultLogProperties(Function<String, @Nullable String> func, String description,
885                                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
886                                super(description, renameKey, order);
887                                this.func = func;
888                        }
889
890                        @Override
891                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
892                                return func.apply(renameKey.apply(key));
893                        }
894
895                }

897        }

914        /**
915         * A log properties that can be mutated like a map.
916         */
917        public interface MutableLogProperties extends LogProperties {
918
919                /**
920                 * Assigns key to a value.
921                 * @param key key.
922                 * @param value value if null will remove the key.
923                 * @return this.
924                 */
925                MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value);

927                /**
928                 * Builder for MutableLogProperties.
929                 * @return builder.
930                 */
931                public static Builder builder() {
932                        return new Builder();
933                }
934
935                /**
936                 * Mutable Log properties builder.
937                 */
938                public final class Builder extends AbstractBuilder<Builder> {
939
940                        private Map<String, String> map = new LinkedHashMap<>();
941
942                        private Builder() {
943                        }
944
945                        @Override
946                        protected Builder self() {
947                                return this;
948                        }
949
950                        /**
951                         * Sets the backing mutable map.
952                         * @param map backing map.
953                         * @return this.
954                         */
955                        public Builder with(Map<String, String> map) {
956                                this.map = map;
957                                return this;
958                        }
959
960                        /**
961                         * Parses a string as {@link Properties} useful for unit testing with Java
962                         * multiline string literal.

964                         * @return this.
965                         */
966                        public Builder copyProperties(String properties) {
967                                map.putAll(PropertiesParser.readProperties(properties));
968                                return this;
969                        }
970
971                        /**
972                         * Builds a mutable log properties.
973                         * @return mutable log properties.
974                         */
975                        public MutableLogProperties build() {
976                                String description = this.description;
977                                if (description == null) {
978                                        description = "custom mutable";
979                                }
980                                var first = new MapLogProperties(map, description, renameKey, order);
981                                if (fallbacks.isEmpty()) {
982                                        return first;
983                                }
984                                List<LogProperties> combined = new ArrayList<>();
985                                combined.add(first);
986                                combined.addAll(fallbacks);
987                                return new CompositeMutableLogProperties(sort(combined));
988                        }
989
990                        private static final class MapLogProperties extends LogProperties.Builder.AbstractLogProperties
991                                        implements MutableLogProperties {
992
993                                private final Map<String, String> map;
994
995                                MapLogProperties(Map<String, String> map, String description, Function<String, String> renameKey,
996                                                int order) {
997                                        super(description, renameKey, order);
998                                        this.map = map;
999                                }
1000
1001                                @Override
1002                                public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1003                                        return map.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1004                                }
1005
1006                                @Override
1007                                public MutableLogProperties put(String key, @Nullable String value) {
1008                                        Objects.requireNonNull(key);
1009                                        key = renameKey.apply(key);
1010                                        if (value == null) {
1011                                                map.remove(key);
1012                                                return this;
1013                                        }
1014                                        map.put(key, value);
1015                                        return this;
1016                                }
1017
1018                        }
1019
1020                }
1021
1022        }

1032        /**
1033         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1034         * use system properties. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and is
1035         * preferred that you get the properties through a config instance instead.</strong>
1036         * @return currently bound properties or system properties.
1037         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1038         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1039         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1040         */
1041        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties() {
1042                return findGlobalProperties(() -> StandardProperties.SYSTEM_PROPERTIES);
1043        }

1045        /**
1046         * Finds global properties by checking the currently bound rainbow gum and if not set
1047         * use the supplier as the fallback. <strong>This method should be used sparingly and
1048         * is preferred that you get the properties through a config instance
1049         * instead.</strong>
1050         * @param fallback supplier to use if no rainbow gum is bound.
1051         * @return currently bound properties or fallback.
1052         * @apiNote the intention of this method is to be used for ServiceLoader singleton
1053         * components and other systems that maybe bound prior to rainbow gum loading that
1054         * need to determine if they should be enabled.
1055         */
1056        public static LogProperties findGlobalProperties(Supplier<? extends LogProperties> fallback) {
1057                var gum = RainbowGum.getOrNull();
1058                if (gum != null) {
1059                        return gum.config().properties();
1060                }
1061                return Objects.requireNonNull(fallback.get());

1064        /**
1065         * Creates log properties from many log properties. Equal properties are only included
1066         * once.
1067         * @param logProperties list of properties.
1068         * @param fallback if the logProperties list is empty.
1069         * @return log properties
1070         */
1071        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties, LogProperties fallback) {
1072                if (logProperties.isEmpty()) {
1073                        return fallback;
1074                }
1075                if (logProperties.size() == 1) {
1076                        return Objects.requireNonNull(logProperties.get(0));
1077                }
1078                var array = sort(logProperties);
1079                return new CompositeLogProperties(array);
1080        }
1081
1082        private static LogProperties[] sort(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1083                @SuppressWarnings("null") // TODO eclipse array issue
1084                LogProperties[] array = logProperties.stream()
1085                        .filter(p -> p != StandardProperties.EMPTY)
1086                        // The same source listed twice adds nothing but noise in reports and errors.
1087                        .distinct()
1088                        .toArray(size -> new LogProperties[size]);
1089                Arrays.sort(array, Comparator.comparingInt(LogProperties::order).reversed());
1090                return array;
1091        }

1094         * Creates log properties from many log properties.

1096         * @return if the logProperties is empty {@link StandardProperties#EMPTY} will be
1097         * used.

1099        public static LogProperties of(List<? extends LogProperties> logProperties) {
1100                return of(logProperties, StandardProperties.EMPTY);

1103        /**

1105         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1106         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1107         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1108         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1109         * properties.
1110         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1111         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1112         * parameters.
1113         */
1114        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties) {

1118        /**
1119         * Creates log properties from a URI query and provided properties. This is useful for
1120         * URI based providers where the URI query is contributing properties for the plugin.
1121         * @param uri query will be used to pull properties from using
1122         * {@link #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)}.
1123         * @param prefix part of the key that will stripped before accessing the URI
1124         * properties.
1125         * @param properties usually this is the properties coming from {@link LogConfig}.
1126         * @param uriKey where the URI came from.
1127         * @return combined properties where properties is tried first than the URI query
1128         * parameters.
1129         */
1130        public static LogProperties of(URI uri, String prefix, LogProperties properties, @Nullable String uriKey) {
1131                /*
1132                 * TODO this should be integrated with the whole providers and registries.
1133                 */
1134                String propDesc = uriKey != null ? "[" + uriKey + "]->" : "";
1135                String description = propDesc + "URI(" + LogRedactor.redactUri(uri) + ")";
1136                var uriProperties = LogProperties.builder()
1137                        .description(description)
1138                        .fromURIQuery(uri)
1139                        .renameKey(s -> LogProperties.removeKeyPrefix(s, prefix))
1140                        .build();
1141                return LogProperties.of(List.of(properties, uriProperties));

1144        /**

1146         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1147         * application/x-www-form-urlencoded </a> format useful for parsing properties values
1148         * that have key values embedded in them. <strong>This parser unlike form encoding
1149         * uses <code>%20</code> for space as the data is coming from a URI.</strong>
1150         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1151         * @param consumer accept will be called for each entry and if key (left hand) does
1152         * not have a "<code>=</code>" following it the second parameter on the consumer
1153         * accept will be passed <code>null</code>.
1154         */
1155        public static void parseUriQuery(String query,
1156                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1157                parseUriQuery(query, true, consumer);
1158        }

1160        /**
1161         * Parses a URI query formatted string to a Map.
1162         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1163         * @return decoded key values with last key winning over previous equal keys.
1164         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1165         */
1166        public static Map<String, String> parseMap(String query) {
1167                Map<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1168                parseUriQuery(query, (k, v) -> {
1169                        if (v != null) {
1170                                m.put(k, v);
1171                        }
1172                });
1173                return m;
1174        }
1175
1176        /**
1177         * Parses a URI query for a multiple value map. The list values of the map maybe empty
1178         * if the query parameter does not have any values associated with it which would be
1179         * the case if there is a parameter (key) with no "<code>=</code>" following it. For
1180         * example the following would have three entries of <code>a,b,c</code> all with empty
1181         * list: <pre>
1182         * <code>
1183         * a&amp;b&amp;c&amp;
1184         * </code> </pre>
1185         * @param query raw query component of URI.
1186         * @return decoded key values with multiple keys grouped together in order found.
1187         * @see #parseUriQuery(String, BiConsumer)
1188         */
1189        public static Map<String, List<String>> parseMultiMap(String query) {
1190                Map<String, List<String>> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1191                BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> f = (k, v) -> {
1192                        List<String> list = Objects.requireNonNull(m.computeIfAbsent(k, _k -> new ArrayList<String>()));
1193                        if (v != null) {
1194                                list.add(v);
1195                        }
1196                };
1197                parseUriQuery(query, f);
1198                return m;
1199        }
1200
1201        /**
1202         * Parses a list of strings from a string that is <a href=
1203         * "https://www.w3.org/TR/2014/REC-html5-20141028/forms.html#url-encoded-form-data">
1204         * percent encoded for escaping (application/x-www-form-urlencoded)</a> where the
1205         * separator can be either "<code>&amp;</code>" or "<code>,</code>".
1206         * <p>
1207         * An example would be using ampersand: <pre><code>
1208         *  "a&amp;b%20B&amp;c" -> ["a","b B","c"]
1209         *  </code> </pre> and comma: <pre><code>
1210         *  "a,b,c" -> ["a","b","c"]
1211         *  </code> </pre>
1212         * <p>
1213         * An element may be empty. One empty element at the start and one at the end are
1214         * dropped, so a value assembled from parts that may be missing still works
1215         * (<code>"a,"</code> and <code>",a,"</code> are <code>["a"]</code>), while every
1216         * other empty element is kept: <pre><code>
1217         *  "" -> []
1218         *  ",," -> [""]
1219         *  "a,,b" -> ["a","","b"]
1220         *  "a,," -> ["a",""]
1221         *  </code> </pre> An equals sign is part of the element: <code>"a=b"</code> is
1222         * <code>["a=b"]</code>.
1223         * @param query the comma or ampersand delimited string.
1224         * @return list of strings
1225         */
1226        public static List<String> parseList(String query) {
1227                List<String> list = new ArrayList<>();
1228                int start = 0;
1229                for (int i = 0; i < query.length(); i++) {
1230                        char c = query.charAt(i);
1231                        if (c == ',' || c == '&') {
1232                                list.add(query.substring(start, i));
1233                                start = i + 1;
1234                        }
1235                }
1236                list.add(query.substring(start));
1237                if (list.get(0).isEmpty()) {
1238                        list.remove(0);
1239                }
1240                if (!list.isEmpty() && list.get(list.size() - 1).isEmpty()) {
1241                        list.remove(list.size() - 1);
1242                }
1243                list.replaceAll(e -> PercentCodec.decode(e, StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
1244                return list;
1245        }
1246
1247        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1248                parseUriQuery(query, decode, "[&,]", consumer);
1249        }
1250
1251        private static void parseUriQuery(String query, boolean decode, String sep,
1252                        BiConsumer<String, @Nullable String> consumer) {
1253                /*
1254                 * TODO default java split has issues but is very fast
1255                 */
1256                @SuppressWarnings("StringSplitter")
1257                String[] pairs = query.split(sep);
1258                for (String pair : pairs) {
1259                        int idx = pair.indexOf("=");
1260                        String key;
1261                        String value;
1262                        if (idx == 0) {
1263                                continue;
1264                        }
1265                        else if (idx < 0) {
1266                                key = pair;
1267                                value = null;
1268                        }
1269                        else {
1270                                key = pair.substring(0, idx);
1271                                value = pair.substring(idx + 1);
1272                        }
1273                        if (decode) {
1274                                key = PercentCodec.decode(key, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1275                                if (value != null) {
1276                                        value = PercentCodec.decode(value, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
1277                                }
1278
1279                        }
1280                        if (key.isBlank()) {
1281                                continue;
1282                        }
1283                        consumer.accept(key, value);
1284                }
1285        }
1286
1287        /**
1288         * Common static log properties such as System properties ane environment variables.
1289         */
1290        @CaseChanging
1291        enum StandardProperties implements LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1292
1293                /**
1294                 * Empty properties. The order is <code>-1</code>.
1295                 */
1296                EMPTY {
1297                        @Override
1298                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1299                                return null;
1300                        }
1301
1302                        @Override
1303                        public int order() {
1304                                return -1;
1305                        }
1306                },
1307                /**
1308                 * Uses {@link System#getProperty(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}. The
1309                 * {@link #order()} is <code>400</code> which the same value as MicroProfile
1310                 * config ordinal.
1311                 */
1312                SYSTEM_PROPERTIES {
1313                        @Override
1314                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1315                                return System.getProperty(key);
1316                        }
1317
1318                        @Override
1319                        public int order() {
1320                                return 400;
1321                        }
1322                },
1323                /**
1324                 * Uses {@link System#getenv(String)} for {@link #valueOrNull(String)}.The
1325                 * {@link #order()} is <code>300</code> which is the same value as MicroProfile
1326                 * config ordinal.
1327                 */
1328                ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES {
1329                        @Override
1330                        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1331                                return System.getenv(translateKey(key));
1332                        }
1333
1334                        @Override
1335                        protected String translateKey(String key) {
1336                                return key.replace(".", "_");
1337                        }
1338
1339                        @Override
1340                        public int order() {
1341                                return 300;
1342                        }
1343                };
1344
1345                @Override
1346                public String description(String key) {
1347                        String k = translateKey(key);
1348                        return name() + "[" + k + "]";
1349                }
1350
1351                /*
1352                 * Each constant's own per-constant class body (see EMPTY/SYSTEM_PROPERTIES/
1353                 * ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES above) makes getClass() an anonymous subclass with no
1354                 * canonical name, so without this LogPropertiesReporting's fallback chain would
1355                 * land on the description(dummyKey) branch instead: name() alone is a cleaner
1356                 * report for the single most common LogProperties in practice (the default when
1357                 * nothing else is configured).
1358                 */
1359                @Override
1360                public void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1361                        out.append(name());
1362                }
1363
1364                /**
1365                 * Translate the key.
1366                 * @param key input
1367                 * @return output
1368                 */
1369                protected String translateKey(String key) {
1370                        return key;
1371                }
1372
1373        }
1374
1375        /**
1376         * Searches a {@value LogProperties#SEP} separated property path recursing up the path
1377         * till a non null value (not missing) is found.
1378         * <p>
1379         * For example assume we have a single property set like
1380         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff=DEBUG</code> and we call this function with
1381         * <code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code>.
1382         * <ol>
1383         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a.b</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1384         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff.a</code> will resolve to <code>null</code></li>
1385         * <li><code>logging.level.com.stuff</code> will resolve to <code>"DEBUG"</code>, stop
1386         * and return <code>"DEBUG"</code>.</li>
1387         * </ol>
1388         * @param <T> type to return.
1389         * @param key the initial path.
1390         * @param resolveFunc function that returns the value at path or <code>null</code>.
1391         * @return value or <code>null</code> if no non null value can be found.
1392         */
1393        @SuppressWarnings("exports")
1394        public static <T extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable T findUpPathOrNull(String key,
1395                        Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc) {
1396                return searchPath(key, resolveFunc, SEP);
1397        }
1398
1399        private static <T> @Nullable T searchPath(String key, Function<String, @Nullable T> resolveFunc, String sep) {
1400                String tempName = key;
1401                @Nullable T level = null;
1402                int indexOfLastDot = tempName.length();
1403                while ((level == null) && (indexOfLastDot > -1)) {
1404                        tempName = tempName.substring(0, indexOfLastDot);
1405                        level = resolveFunc.apply(tempName);
1406                        indexOfLastDot = tempName.lastIndexOf(sep);
1407                }
1408                if (level != null) {
1409                        return level;
1410                }
1411                return resolveFunc.apply("");
1412        }
1413
1414        /**
1415         * Concats a key using {@link #SEP} to the root prefix.
1416         * @param name key.
1417         * @return concat key.
1418         */
1419        static String concatKey(String name) {
1420                return concatKey(LogProperties.ROOT_PREFIX, name);
1421        }
1422
1423        /**
1424         * Concats a keys using {@link #SEP} as the separator.
1425         * @param prefix start of key.
1426         * @param name second part of key.
1427         * @return key.
1428         */
1429        static String concatKey(String prefix, String name) {
1430                if (name.equals("")) {
1431                        return prefix;
1432                }
1433                if (prefix.equals("")) {
1434                        return name;
1435                }
1436                if (prefix.endsWith(".")) {
1437                        prefix = prefix.substring(0, prefix.length() - 1);
1438                }
1439                if (name.startsWith(SEP)) {
1440                        return prefix + name;
1441                }
1442                return prefix + SEP + name;
1443        }
1444
1445        /**
1446         * Replace "{name}" tokens in property names.
1447         * @param key property name.
1448         * @param parameters tokens to replace with entry values.
1449         * @return interpolated property key.
1450         * @see #interpolateKey(String, Function)
1451         */
1452        static String interpolateKey(String key, Map<String, String> parameters) {
1453                return interpolateKey(key, parameters::get);
1454        }
1455
1456        /**
1457         * Replaces property <strong>key</strong> parameters by using the lookup function.
1458         * Property keys are often parameterized usually by some name. The parameters are
1459         * surrounded by curly braces and replaced by the lookup function. An example of the
1460         * format is <code>a.{PARAM}</code> which has a parameter named <code>PARAM</code>. If
1461         * the lookup function has <code>PARAM->b</code> then the result will be
1462         * <code>a.b</code>. If a value for a parameter is null (indicates not found) an
1463         * exception is thrown.
1464         * @param key to be interpolated.
1465         * @param lookup function that may return null for a parameter.
1466         * @return interpolated key with all parameters replaced.
1467         * @throws IllegalArgumentException if the lookup function does not have a value for a
1468         * parameter.
1469         */
1470        public static String interpolateKey(String key,
1471                        @SuppressWarnings("exports") Function<String, ? extends @Nullable String> lookup)
1472                        throws IllegalArgumentException {
1473                var parameters = keyParameters(key);
1474                String result = key;
1475                for (String k : parameters) {
1476                        var v = lookup.apply(k);
1477                        if (v == null) {
1478                                throw new IllegalArgumentException(
1479                                                "Keyed parameter missing. key: '" + key + "' parameter: '" + k + "'");
1480                        }
1481                        LogProperty.Validator.validateKeyParameterValue(key, k, v);
1482                        result = result.replace("{" + k + "}", v);
1483                }
1484                return result;
1485        }
1486
1487        /**
1488         * Interpolates a named key which is a property key that has a {@value #NAME}.
1489         * @param key with name parameters.
1490         * @param name replace name token.
1491         * @return interpolated property key.
1492         */
1493        static String interpolateNamedKey(String key, String name) {
1494                return interpolateKey(key, Map.of(NAME, name));
1495        }
1496
1497        /**
1498         * Remove key prefix from the key. Prefix should end in "." but this method does not
1499         * check that.
1500         * @param key key whose prefix will be removed.
1501         * @param prefix property name prefix.
1502         * @return prefix removed if the string is prefixed.
1503         */
1504        static String removeKeyPrefix(String key, String prefix) {
1505                if (key.startsWith(prefix)) {
1506                        return key.substring(prefix.length());
1507                }
1508                return key;
1509        }
1510
1511        /**
1512         * Property prefix parameter pattern.
1513         */
1514        static final Pattern PARAMETER_PATTERN = Pattern.compile("\\{(.*?)\\}");
1515
1516        /**
1517         * Extract key parameters with {@link #PARAMETER_PATTERN}.
1518         * @param key also known as property name.
1519         * @return parameters in key.
1520         */
1521        static Set<String> keyParameters(String key) {
1522                Set<String> tokens = new LinkedHashSet<>();
1523                Matcher matcher = PARAMETER_PATTERN.matcher(key);
1524                while (matcher.find()) {
1525                        var t = matcher.group(1);
1526                        if (t == null) {
1527                                throw new IllegalStateException("bug with parameter pattern regex.");
1528                        }
1529                        tokens.add(t);
1530                }
1531                return tokens;
1532        }
1533
1534        /**
1535         * Validate key parameters.
1536         * @param key key to be interpolated with parameters.
1537         * @param parameters names of parameters which must <strong>equal</strong> the set of
1538         * the found parameters. while the order obviously does not matter the set cannot have
1539         * more parameters than found in the key.
1540         */
1541        static void validateKeyParameters(String key, Set<String> parameters) {
1542                var keyParameters = keyParameters(key);
1543                if (!parameters.equals(keyParameters)) {
1544                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Keyed parameter mismatch. key: '" + key + "' , key parameters: "
1545                                        + keyParameters + " provided parameters: " + parameters);
1546                }
1547        }
1548
1549        /**
1550         * Standard way to produce description for a key.
1551         * @param type the properties type name.
1552         * @param key the properties key translated.
1553         * @return description for key.
1554         */
1555        static String descriptionForKey(String type, String key) {
1556                return type + "[" + key + "]";
1557        }
1558
1559        /**
1560         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1561         * similar), without a line number.
1562         * @param type the properties type name.
1563         * @param resource file like name.
1564         * @param key the properties key translated.
1565         * @return description for key.
1566         */
1567        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key) {
1568                return type + "[" + resource + "][" + key + "]";
1569        }
1570
1571        /**
1572         * Standard way to produce description for a key found in a resource (a file or
1573         * similar) at a known index, usually a line number.
1574         * @param type the properties type name.
1575         * @param resource file like name.
1576         * @param key the properties key translated.
1577         * @param index usually line number of where key found.
1578         * @return description for key.
1579         */
1580        static String descriptionForResource(String type, String resource, String key, long index) {
1581                return type + "[" + resource + ":" + index + "][" + key + "]";
1582        }
1583
1584}

1586final class MultiMapProperties extends AbstractLogProperties {
1587
1588        private final Map<String, List<String>> multiMap;
1589
1590        public MultiMapProperties(Map<String, List<String>> multiMap, String description,
1591                        Function<String, String> renameKey, int order) {
1592                super(description, renameKey, order);
1593                this.multiMap = multiMap;
1594        }
1595
1596        @Override
1597        public @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1598                return _valueOrNull(renameKey.apply(key));
1599        }
1600
1601        private @Nullable String _valueOrNull(String key) {
1602                var list = multiMap.get(key);
1603                if (list == null || list.isEmpty()) {
1604                        return null;
1605                }
1606                return list.get(0);
1607        }
1608
1609        @Override
1610        public @Nullable List<String> listOrNull(String key) {
1611                return multiMap.get(renameKey.apply(key));
1612        }
1613
1614        @Override
1615        public @Nullable Map<String, String> mapOrNull(String key) {
1616                String s = valueOrNull(key);
1617                if (s != null) {
1618                        return LogProperties.parseMap(s);
1619                }
1620                var map = PropertyMaps.fromKeys(this, key);
1621                if (map != null) {
1622                        return map;
1623                }
1624                /*
1625                 * Now we check for dotted notation since key was not set. key.subkey=value
1626                 */
1627                String prefix = renameKey.apply(key) + LogProperties.SEP;
1628                LinkedHashMap<String, String> m = new LinkedHashMap<>();
1629                for (var k : multiMap.keySet()) {
1630                        if (k.startsWith(prefix) && !k.equals(prefix)) {
1631                                String v = _valueOrNull(k);
1632                                if (v != null) {
1633                                        String _k = k.substring(prefix.length());
1634                                        m.put(_k, v);
1635                                }
1636                        }
1637                }
1638                return m.isEmpty() ? null : m;
1639        }
1640
1641}
1642
1643interface ListLogProperties extends LogProperties, LogReporter.Reportable {
1644
1645        @Override
1646        default @Nullable String valueOrNull(String key) {
1647                for (var props : properties()) {
1648                        var value = props.valueOrNull(key);
1649                        if (value != null) {
1650                                return value;
1651                        }
1652                }
1653                return null;
1654        }
1655
1656        @Override
1657        default <R extends @Nullable Object> @Nullable R visit(String key,
1658                        BiFunction<LogProperties, String, @Nullable R> visitor) {
1659                for (var props : properties()) {
1660                        var value = props.visit(key, visitor);
1661                        if (value != null) {
1662                                return value;
1663                        }
1664                }
1665                return null;
1666        }
1667
1668        @Override
1669        default String description(String key) {
1670                var descriptions = new ArrayList<String>();
1671                visit(key, (source, sourceKey) -> {
1672                        descriptions.add(source.description(sourceKey));
1673                        return null;
1674                });
1675                String description = String.join(", ", descriptions);
1676                if (description.length() > 120) {
1677                        return "\n    " + String.join(",\n    ", descriptions);
1678                }
1679                return description;
1680        }
1681
1682        LogProperties[] properties();
1683
1684        default StringBuilder toString(StringBuilder sb) {
1685                sb.append(getClass().getSimpleName());
1686                sb.append("[properties=").append(Arrays.deepToString(properties())).append("]");
1687                return sb;
1688        }
1689
1690        /*
1691         * Reports components separated by commas without the error description's line
1692         * wrapping (via LogPropertiesReporting.describe, the same fallback chain
1693         * LogReporter#appendGlobalProperties uses for the top level LogProperties a LogConfig
1694         * was built with) rather than per key.
1695         */
1696        @Override
1697        default void report(Appendable out) throws IOException {
1698                boolean first = true;
1699                for (var p : properties()) {
1700                        if (first) {
1701                                first = false;
1702                        }
1703                        else {
1704                                out.append(", ");
1705                        }
1706                        LogPropertiesReporting.describe(out, p);
1707                }
1708        }
1709
1710}
1711
1712/*
1713 * Shared by ListLogProperties#report(Appendable) (recursively, per component) and
1714 * LogReporter's own appendGlobalProperties(Appendable, LogProperties) (for the top level
1715 * LogProperties a LogConfig was built with), so there is exactly one fallback chain for
1716 * "how do we describe an arbitrary LogProperties for a report": an explicit
1717 * Reportable#report(...) if implemented, else the concrete class' fully qualified name
1718 * (stable and free: no override needed), else, only for the rare case where the FQCN
1719 * itself is null (e.g. one of StandardProperties' own per constant enum bodies, which are
1720 * anonymous classes under the hood, before it implemented Reportable directly),
1721 * description(key) with a dummy key, since that is the only description() such a
1722 * LogProperties is guaranteed to answer at all.
1723 */
1724final class LogPropertiesReporting {
1725
1726        static final String DESCRIBE_KEY = "logging.reporter.describe";
1727
1728        private LogPropertiesReporting() {
1729        }
1730
1731        static void describe(Appendable out, LogProperties properties) throws IOException {
1732                if (properties instanceof LogReporter.Reportable r) {
1733                        r.report(out);
1734                        return;
1735                }
1736                String fqcn = properties.getClass().getCanonicalName();
1737                if (fqcn != null) {
1738                        out.append(fqcn);
1739                        return;
1740                }
1741                out.append(properties.description(DESCRIBE_KEY));
1742        }
1743
1744}
